<reason>A won the central comparison between greater liability and existing fault-based responsibility. B established plausible company-level precautions, but did not convincingly explain why ordinary negligence could not require them. Its decisive claims that safeguards are barely tried and their omission is always excused were unsupported. A answered the pressure directly and better explained the limits of both technological prevention and B's compensation rationale.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A effectively pressed B's exemption for operators using reasonable safeguards: the proposed duties largely matched the negligence A already accepted, while careful operators' exemption left the vanished-rider compensation problem unresolved. B's appeal to a higher, specific duty did not establish why that expansion improved on A's boundary.</best_rebuttal>
